# Draft:Warfe Engracia

----
'Dr. Warfe Tupas Engracia (Born - June 1, 1942) is a Filipino physician specializing in radiology and diagnostic sonology. He has practiced medicine in the Philippines and abroad for more than five decades. In addition to his medical career, he has been involved in cultural advocacy related to Indigenous heritage and ethnolinguistic communities in the Philippines.'
Early life
Dr. Engracia was born in 1946 in the town of Initao, Misamis Oriental, Philippines. He has stated that he traces his ancestry to Rajah Tupas, historically described as the last Rajah of Cebu prior to Spanish colonization.
Education
Dr. Engracia earned his Doctor of Medicine degree from Southwestern University – Matias H. Aznar Memorial College of Medicine in April 1969. He passed the Philippine Medical Licensure Examination in August 1969.
From 1970 to 1973, he completed diagnostic training in radiology at Sacred Heart Hospital and Southwestern University MHAM College of Medicine in Cebu City.
He undertook postgraduate studies in radiology with the Royal Australasian College of Radiologists in New Zealand from 1976 to 1980, rotating through Auckland Hospital, Princess Mary Hospital, Greenlane Hospital, National Women’s Hospital, and Middlemore Hospital.
In May 1984, he completed advanced training in diagnostic ultrasound at the Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori and the National Cancer Institute in Milan, Italy. He later completed additional ultrasound and bone densitometry training in the United States and Southeast Asia between 1996 and 1997.
Medical career
Dr. Engracia has practiced medicine for over 55 years, specializing in radiology and sonology.
From 1970 to 1976, he served as a faculty member in the Radiology Section of MHAM College of Medicine, Southwestern University, and as a radiologist at Medina General Hospital in Ozamiz City.
Between 1976 and 1980, he trained as a radiology registrar in New Zealand. He was registered as a medical practitioner in Papua New Guinea in 1981.
From 1982 to 1987, Engracia held chairman roles in X-ray departments at hospitals in Saudi Arabia, including Almana General Hospital in Al Khobar and King Khaled International Airport Hospital in Riyadh.
He served as consultant radiologist for the Ministry of Health of Kuwait from June 1989 to August 1990.
From 1991 to 1998, he was Chairman of the X-Ray Department at Cebu City Medical Center, and from 1993 to 1997, he served as Chairman and Radiologist at St. Vincent General Hospital in Cebu City.
Between 1994 and 1997, Warfe was a member and vice chairman of the Board of Examiners of the Philippine Board of Radiology.
He has operated diagnostic imaging centers under Rajah Tupas Medical Services since 2004, including facilities at Elizabeth Mall, Cebu City, Mandaue City, and Pinamungajan, Cebu. These facilities are licensed by the Food and Drug Administration (Philippines) to operate medical X-ray services.
From 2012 onward, he has served as a radiologist and sonologist at multiple medical laboratories and clinics in Cebu Province.
Advocacy and Cultural Work
Beyond medicine, Dr. Engracia has been involved in cultural preservation and Indigenous advocacy in the Philippines. His activities include support for ethnolinguistic heritage initiatives and participation in community-based cultural engagement programs.
He has maintained professional and cultural ties with organizations and communities in Malaysia, including participation as a Philippine representative at cultural and literary events, such as the Langkawi International Writers Festival in October 2023.
Honors and Recognition
Dr. Engracia has received several recognitions in medicine, arts, and culture, including:
* 2017 – Conferred Doctor of Humanities (Honoris Causa), Northwestern Christian University, Florida, USA
* 2018 – Named Cebu City’s Most Outstanding Individual during the city’s 81st Founding Anniversary
* 2019 – Awarded Doctor of Philosophy in Transformational Leadership, Northwestern Christian University
* 2019 – Received the Distinguished Service Cross (Gold) from the Knights of Rizal, 22nd International Assembly
* 2024 – Named one of the Ten Outstanding Cebuano (TOCA) in Arts and Culture
* 2024 – Recognized as Asian Modern Hero in the Medical Field
Selected Works
* The STUMP (2021)
* Featuring Rajah Tupas, Rizal and I (2021)
* Thermal Collision for COVID-19 (2021)
